counterexample: Tick spacing 10. Start 100, end 100, an empty range. The current tick is set to 101 before the empty-range return, so hasNext is true and getNext returns 101, a tick that is not initialized and not a multiple of the spacing. The walk should return nothing, and hasNext should be false straight away. The functional test test_iterateDown_emptyRange fails for this reason.

new_flaw.description: Every taxed zero-for-one swap that stays inside one tick walks the tick start + 1, which it never crossed. When that tick is initialized, the hook subtracts its net liquidity and adds reward growth to it. This happens for any tick in a spacing-1 pool, or when the pool sits one tick below a multiple of the spacing. Example: spacing 1, pool at tick 500 with active liquidity L1, and a position whose lower tick is 501 with liquidity L2 smaller than L1. A taxed swap that stays at tick 500 makes the reward walk divide the leftover tax by L1 - L2 instead of L1, so in-range positions are credited more than the tax collected. With L2 larger than L1 the subtraction underflows and the swap reverts.

summary: Sets the current tick to the start tick plus one before the empty-range check. Non-empty walks now include the start tick, but an empty range no longer gives hasNext false.
